title: Introduce semantic-prioritized regression gate with cohort scheduler and budget-aware replay
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Adds a semantic-prioritized regression gate and a cohort scheduler to stagger replays and reduce flakiness during CI. No API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed several recent false-positive regressions where syntactically small but semantically important prompts triggered noisy failures in CI. This PR introduces a semantic-prioritized regression gate that weights prompt-set regressions by an embedding-based semantic distance and prompt metadata priors, and pairs it with a cohort scheduler that makes replay/rollback work budget-aware and less bursty.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Implements a new gate module eval_harness.gates.semantic_priority_gate that computes a per-prompt priority score combining semantic drift (cosine distance of anchor embeddings), historical volatility (per-prompt stability index), and metadata priors (owner, sensitivity). High-priority prompts will cause stricter thresholds and faster escalation; low-priority prompts are subject to progressive attenuation (delayed alerts, larger tolerances). Adds a cohort scheduler service eval_harness.orchestration.cohort_scheduler which: (a) staggers replay execution windows to avoid thundering replays against shared models, (b) enforces a configurable daily budget per-linear-ticket/owner, (c) respects dynamic drift signals (samples more aggressively when drift magnitude > threshold). Integrates the gate into CI via ci/hooks/semantic_priority_gate.yml and exposes detailed metrics to observability via eval_harness.metrics.semantic_gate.* (priority_histogram, triggered_alerts_total, replay_budget_utilization). Includes a small opt-in web UI patch for console devs at docs/snippets/semantic-gate-usage.md showing how to configure per-team priors.

Design notes and rationale: The primary signal is embedding-based cosine distance against a stabilized anchor per-prompt; we use a rolling median of recent embeddings to reduce noise. Priority score = alpha * normalized_cosine + beta * volatility + gamma * prior_score; coefficients are configurable via env or console. The scheduler deliberately biases toward avoiding overlapping heavy replays on the same model region to keep token spikes under SLA. We calibrated the default budget to 5% of daily smoke evaluation capacity for non-critical teams.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed lint and an intermittent test in test_cohort_scheduler (timing-dependent). I fixed the race by adding a small deterministic sleep/wait condition and adjusted mocks to freeze time in unit tests. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, integration-local, lint); alerting on flaky integration tests added to flaky-tests LABEL for follow-up.
